lede: The biggest thing on the civic calendar this week is Tuesday's BOCC meeting, where the county is voting on two Land Use Code amendments — one updating rules for natural medicine businesses, the other on nonconforming lots, the kind of quiet code language that shapes what gets built where for years. That same day, HARC takes up the Carhenge redevelopment at 700 W Pacific Ave, three large-scale public hearings covering eight new buildings in an Accommodations 2 zone. Wednesday brings the county's sixth working session on its housing code rewrite, drilling into zoning density, new workforce housing types, and the regulatory incentives that could actually move the needle on affordability.
